synopsis: ISO 10265:2008 is identified as the brake-performance and testing standard for crawler machines at 20 km/h or less, distinct from ISO 3450 for wheeled and fast rubber-tracked machines; it was confirmed in 2025 [f5979, f13728, f15189, f5980]. Stopping performance is measured from brake-control actuation to standstill, including system response but excluding operator reaction, with prescribed payload and adverse test configurations [f6540]. ISO 17757 uses physical braking and steering tests in manual and autonomous modes under ISO 3450 and ISO 10265, and the booklet found no simulation wording in those brake standards [f7734, f15197]. These are machine-performance standards rather than statistical model-transfer standards, and they provide no defensible calibration-stop count guaranteeing braking predictions across 100-plus site types, brake architectures and weather conditions [f6163, f6162, f15198]. There is an unresolved evidence tension: later chapters and the glossary make specific scope and testing claims, while Chapters 3 and 13 say ISO 10265 was not verified in the research [f2197, f11197, f5979, f7734, f15192].
